# Activity coefficients from the Van Laar model for the water-nitric-sulfuric acid system

`eos.van_laar_acid_activity_coefficients`

## Source

**Taleb, D.; Ponche, J. L.; Mirabel, P. (1996)**

Journal of Geophysical Research 101(D20), 25967-25977

DOI: [10.1029/96JD02155](https://doi.org/10.1029/96JD02155)


## What this model is

A **direct** model: a computation over vectors, with no iteration and therefore no algorithm block. It is here because a calculation's inputs are scalars, so a composition vector has nowhere in the calc registry to go - and it is a model rather than a library function so that it goes through the spec-driven pipeline like everything else.

## Inputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `components` | - | the substances the mixture is made of, by name; water, nitric acid and sulfuric acid (`hno3`, `h2so4`) are the three the model covers, and any other name is a species it does not |
| `T` | K | absolute temperature |
| `x` | dimensionless | mole fractions; non-negative and summing to one. |


## Outputs

| Name | Unit | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ln_gamma` | dimensionless | the natural logarithm of the activity coefficient of each component |
| `gamma` | dimensionless | the activity coefficient of each component |

| Bound | On violation | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `T > 0` | raises | an absolute temperature; zero and below are not states |
| `T >= 190 and T <= 298` | warns `OUT_OF_VALID_RANGE` | the Taleb correlation is fitted from 190 K to 298 K; outside it the model extrapolates. |

## Assumptions

- this is NeqSim's `ComponentGEVanLaarAcid`, the acid-specific Van Laar model of Taleb, Ponche and Mirabel (1996). NeqSim 3.20.0 has no classical fitted-`A12`/`A21` Van Laar.

- the three species are water, nitric acid and sulfuric acid, in that order, and they are evaluated on their own mole-fraction basis: only those three fractions in `x` enter the ternary expression, so a dissolved carrier gas does not.

- that basis is renormalised to sum to one, which is the form of the port source and does not move the answer: each expression is homogeneous of degree zero in the three fractions, so any scaling of them returns the same activity coefficient.

- a component outside the three gets a `gamma` of `1.0e12` rather than a refusal. That is NeqSim's `NON_MODELED_COMPONENT_PENALTY` reproduced: a device for pushing an uncovered species out of the liquid phase, not a physical activity coefficient, so the `ln_gamma` beside it is finite but meaningless.

- a mixture with no acid at all is evaluated on pure water, which is what NeqSim's `acidMoleFractions` returns for an empty basis.

- every logarithm in the model is base-10, and `T` is in Kelvin throughout; the source is valid from about 190 K to 298 K, and a temperature outside that is reported as a warning rather than refused.

- `eos.ge_van_laar_acid_phase` is the phase this belongs to: it composes this with `eos.nitric_sulfuric_acid_vapor_pressure` and ports `ComponentGEVanLaarAcid.fugcoef`, the override that forces the Raoult reference.

- `x` is checked (non-negative, sums to one) rather than renormalised.

## References

- Taleb, D.; Ponche, J. L.; Mirabel, P. (1996). "Vapor pressures in the ternary system water-nitric acid-sulfuric acid at low temperature." Journal of Geophysical Research 101(D20), 25967-25977.
- NeqSim - https://github.com/equinor/neqsim - Apache-2.0. `ComponentGEVanLaarAcid` and `NitricSulfuricAcidVaporPressure` are the port source; the latter documents an engineering adjustment to its pure-HNO3 vapour pressure coefficients, which is not ported because the vapour pressure is not.
